reference_sql:
SELECT product_id, category_id, unit_cost_eur,
       DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY unit_cost_eur) AS cost_level
FROM products
WHERE category_id BETWEEN 35 AND 40
alternatives:
SELECT p.product_id, p.category_id, p.unit_cost_eur,
       1 + (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p2.unit_cost_eur) FROM products p2
            WHERE p2.category_id = p.category_id AND p2.unit_cost_eur < p.unit_cost_eur) AS cost_level
FROM products p
WHERE p.category_id BETWEEN 35 AND 40

SELECT p.product_id, p.category_id, p.unit_cost_eur, COUNT(DISTINCT p2.unit_cost_eur) + 1 AS cost_level
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN products p2 ON p2.category_id = p.category_id AND p2.unit_cost_eur < p.unit_cost_eur
WHERE p.category_id BETWEEN 35 AND 40
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.category_id, p.unit_cost_eur

other_way.sql:
SELECT p.product_id, p.category_id, p.unit_cost_eur,
       1 + (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p2.unit_cost_eur) FROM products p2
            WHERE p2.category_id = p.category_id AND p2.unit_cost_eur < p.unit_cost_eur) AS cost_level
FROM products p
WHERE p.category_id BETWEEN 35 AND 40
other_way.tradeoff: Counting the different cheaper costs gives the same level on any engine, but it reads the table again for every product.
